hook.description: Catherine steps hard on the herbarium book.
hook.evidence: The aggressive, deliberate destruction of a personal item immediately establishes the villain's cruelty.

candidates.reason: The immediate framing of an innocent maid for poisoning creates high stakes and instant conflict.

hook.description: The Duchess points an accusing finger at her own son.
hook.evidence: A bedridden matriarch accusing her son of poisoning her is a powerful, high-drama hook.

candidates.reason: The betrayal of a mother by her son provides a compelling emotional hook for new viewers.

hook.description: Extreme close-up of the name 'Juliana Ashcroft' in the book.
hook.evidence: The reveal of a secret noble identity is a classic trope that hooks viewers interested in 'hidden identity' dramas.

candidates.reason: The exposure of a secret noble identity combined with the villain's taunting creates immediate tension.

hook.description: Rupert orders the guard to drag Juliana to the wet cells.
hook.evidence: The immediate threat of imprisonment and the gallows creates a sense of urgency.

candidates.reason: The finality of the order to the gallows leaves the viewer desperate to know if she survives.
